pr_open: A real pull request, opened by an agent. Git finds no conflict.
pr_comment: The memory review reads it as graph facts. It names the contradiction and the path that proves it.
pr_check: The required memory-review check fails, so main does not take this merge.
live_hero: The same review runs live in a web page. Nothing to install.
real_open: Now on real data. Pick any public GitHub repository.
real_blocked: One agent read it a year ago, another reads it today. Relate blocks every value that moved.
real_links: Each fact links to the exact file and commit on GitHub it was read from.
real_fix: Mark the new facts as replacing the old ones. The review passes.
real_graph: The real repository as a Relate graph: each service, its facts and the files behind them.
play_open: Write a memory yourself. Say payments-api uses mysql-8. Relate blocks it in the page.
play_fix1: Replace the old fact. Three facts rest on it, so the review still blocks.
play_github: Now make it real: Open it on GitHub. The server starts one workflow and GitHub's bot opens it.
play_real: A minute later it is a real pull request, and memory-review passed.
live_stale: A stale clone. Git merges it cleanly. The graph loses a note and its links.
